[img]https://i.imgur.com/Z4GOv8H.png[/img]
When a pawn from an enemy faction dies it adds to a cooldown timer for the faction to be able to raid again. By default, each death adds 12 hours, up to a maximum of 360 hours (15 days). The amount of time per death and maximum cooldown are configurable through the mod settings menu. This is essentially a light-weight version of my older mod:  [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2006644524]Faction Resources[/url].


[h1]Extra Features[/h1]
[list]
[*]Maximum cooldown time and time added per death are configurable.
[*]Option to display a faction's current cooldown on the faction screen.
[/list]

[h1]Recommended Mods[/h1]
Highly recommended to use with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2006638530]Enemy Self Preservation[/url]. Without it, enemy factions will take greater losses during raids and lead to higher average cooldown times. 


[h1]Mod Compatibility[/h1]
[list]
[*]Not compatible with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2006644524]Faction Resources[/url].
[*]Maybe compatible with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2222935097]Rim War[/url]?
[/list]

mods.name: Keep Converting
mods.author: Linnun
mods.description:
You know the struggle: You use your Moral Guide's "Convert" ability to reduce a pawn's certainty, but then forget to repeat the process when the cooldown wears off. By the time you remember, the target has regained way too much certainty.
	
Worry no longer! With this mod you can set a target for your Moral Guide to Keep Converting, and they'll automatically perform the Convert action on that pawn whenever it's off cooldown – until the target is successfully converted, or becomes invalid (e.g., dead, left map, etc.).

mods.name: Layered Apparel
mods.author: Costel
mods.description:
Give each colonist a personal style, or apply a shared uniform to a whole group. Cosmetics change how apparel looks while keeping actual equipment and its stats intact.

Features:
- Appearance editing: Adjust colors, and set size, position, and rotation separately for the front, sides, and back. Preview all four directions together or inspect one at a larger size.
- Layer control: Reorder cosmetics and fine-tune their rendering offsets.
- Separate cosmetic lists: Configure default, drafted, vacuum, and Exosuit pilot appearances.
- Display conditions: Show cosmetics all the time, link them to specific equipment, or match worn equipment by apparel layers, body coverage, and minimum armor ratings.
- Cosmetic Manager: Edit colonists and presets in one place. Save, overwrite, or delete presets, and apply configurations from a colonist or preset to multiple colonists at once.
- Selective application: Choose which cosmetic lists and items to apply, preview the result on a recipient, and replace the selected lists or add to them.
- Equipment tools: Copy a worn item's HEX color code, add it as a cosmetic, or add it with an equipment link.

Requires Harmony. Vacuum cosmetics use Odyssey; pilot cosmetics use Exosuit Framework. Both are optional for the other features.

Safe to add or remove mid-game.

mods.name: Meaningful Encounters
mods.author: SirDarkElf
mods.description:
Turn strangers into recurring characters.

When a peaceful visitor, trader or refugee is on your map, you can toggle Interaction on them. Your colonists (with Warden priority) will then socialize with them - just like they would with a prisoner. Chat, insult, deep talk, whatever comes up. Toggle also works on hostile pawns like raiders, but has no effect while they're actively hostile - it just marks them, so if one gets captured and later released, the interaction system is already active.

Once they've become at least an acquaintance to one of your colonists, that pawn is remembered. They stay in your colonist's social tab even after leaving. And - with a configurable chance - they show up again in future events. As a caravan member, a wanderer, a rescued crash survivor, or even a raider. Their identity, traits and shared memories persist. Their faction may change: they lived their own life while you were apart.

Family members left behind at character creation are automatically remembered. So are the backstory relatives of your colonists.

Remembered pawns can appear in any role, even combat roles they aren't really suited for. Your peaceful trader friend might turn up as a raider one day, fumbling with a gun. This makes raids feel less like anonymous soldier waves and more like a small persistent world where people you know might be on the other side. Be warned: this can shift combat balance. A raid party may include a couple of pawns who aren't real fighters, which lowers the difficulty of that particular encounter. If you prefer strict combat balance, this mod is probably not for you. If you prefer stories with faces, it might be exactly what you're looking for.

You can mark pawns as "important" or "forget" them from the social tab. Forgotten pawns fade away over 8 in-game hours.

Configurable in Mod Settings: chance for a remembered pawn to be picked when an event generates a new one. Default 20%.

Compatibility: Likely conflicts with mods that also modify PawnGenerator's redress logic, such as Reunion. Should work fine with most other mods.

Requires Harmony.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/iCj5o7O.png[/img]

Will generate missing icons for ChemicalDefs so they do not get the default "missing icon" when autogenerated into possible genes.

All added chemicals in the game will generate three genes for drug-addicition and resistance. If the mod does not also add icons for these chemicals they will generate an error the first time they are visible in the game and instead use the default icon for missing texture.

This mod iterates through all chemicals on game-start and for all genes based on that chemical it checks if the icon is missing. If so it generates an icon based on the default gene-icons for drugs overlayed with the icon of the first registered drug in the game that uses the chemical.

mods.description:
Commissioned RimWorld mod to optimize Ideology creation on large mod lists

Generating required Ideology apparel for roles takes a lot of time on large modlists with high amount of new apparel items, which causes the game to freeze on each modification of the ideology structure and/or memes.

This mod bypasses that by simply disabling automatic apparel generation for these roles.
